overview.title: Intelligence + Continual Learning = Expertise
overview.speaker: Yu Su
overview.main_topic: The distinction between intelligence and expertise in AI agents, and how continual learning bridges the gap.
overview.executive_summary: Yu Su discusses the evolutionary stage of AI agents, highlighting that while foundational models possess high general intelligence (inference-time reasoning, solving from context), they lack situated expertise required for reliable everyday digital work across specialized micro-worlds. He introduces the formula Intelligence + Continual Learning = Expertise, framing continual learning as adaptive compression of experience into reusable structures, leading to unbounded expertise from bounded intelligence.
overview.purpose: To provide a conceptual distinction between raw intelligence and situated expertise in AI agents, and to argue for the necessity of continual learning to build reliable enterprise and personal AI assistants.

topic_map.explanation: Tracing AI agents from logical agents (1960s-80s) and neural agents (2010s) to modern multimodal language agents, emphasizing increasing expressiveness, reasoning, and adaptability.
key_claims: AI agents are not new, but early iterations captured very limited facets of human intelligence.
Language agents have found their first mass market in coding because code is a language-native, symbolic world.
examples: Anthropic's annualized run rate growth driven largely by coding and coding-related productivity capabilities.
topic_map.why_it_matters: Explains why AI has succeeded in coding while struggling in messy everyday digital environments.

topic_map.explanation: Comparing symbolic reasoning (hard things made easy for AI) with everyday digital work like planning, grounding, world modeling, and social norms (easy things made hard for AI).
key_claims: Modern society consists of millions of heterogeneous micro-worlds (professions, organizations, software systems) with unique local physics.
Monolithic models cannot compress this heterogeneity into a single static representation.
examples: MIT report showing 95% of generative AI pilots at companies failing due to brittle errors in enterprise settings.
topic_map.why_it_matters: Highlights why foundation models fail when leaving the privileged world of code.

topic_map.explanation: Defining intelligence as the capacity to reason through unfamiliar problems from available context, and expertise as accumulated and situated competence.
key_claims: Intelligence expands search and can be rented; expertise compresses search and must be learned in situ.
Experts see the world differently through pattern recognition, deep structure understanding, conditional knowledge, and judgment/taste.
examples: Meeting scheduling viewed as a constraint optimization problem over authority, urgency, and dependencies rather than just finding open slots.
topic_map.why_it_matters: Establishes that knowing more facts is insufficient; AI needs situated world models.

topic_map.explanation: Framing continual learning as adaptive compression of experience into reusable structure for future behavior.
key_claims: Continual learning is the crucial bridge from intelligence to expertise.
Different continual learning algorithms set the slope of the learning curve relative to raw intelligence.
examples: Embedding, indexing, distillation, and reinforcement learning used for compression.
topic_map.why_it_matters: Provides a formal definition and framework for how AI agents can improve on the job.

key_points.explanation: Intelligence is general and inference-time; expertise is situated, accumulated over time, and domain-specific.
key_points.evidence: Frontier models excel at unfamiliar problem solving via context but lack localized operational reliability.
key_points.practical_implication: Deploying AI in enterprise requires building systems that learn continually rather than relying solely on base model scale.

key_points.explanation: Without continual learning, scaling intelligence yields the world's smartest novice that brute-forces every problem.
key_points.evidence: Graph of Expertise vs. Raw Intelligence showing strong continual learning achieving exponential escape expertise.
key_points.practical_implication: Investing in continual learning algorithms unlocks unbounded expertise from bounded intelligence.

frameworks.name: The Expertise Framework
frameworks.how_it_works: Combines pattern recognition, deep structure navigation, conditional knowledge, and judgment/taste.
frameworks.when_to_use: When evaluating whether an AI agent is ready for complex, multi-step enterprise or personal workflows.

frameworks.name: Continual Learning Definition Framework
frameworks.how_it_works: Breaks continual learning down into experience inputs, compression methods, target structures, and usage modes.
frameworks.when_to_use: When designing agentic memory and learning architectures.

examples.what_happened: MIT report finding 95% of generative AI pilots at companies failing.
examples.illustrates: The fragility of AI agents when leaving the privileged world of code and entering unstructured micro-worlds.
examples.lesson: AI needs robust situated expertise and continual learning, not just general intelligence.

immediate: Recognize the critical gap between general model intelligence and domain-specific situated expertise.
Evaluate AI agent architectures for memory and continual learning capabilities.
strategic: Shift engineering focus from raw model scaling to continual learning loops that build institutional memory.
Target micro-world specialization to lower economic friction and unlock new domains of work.
questions_to_investigate: How to measure expertise in a domain-specific manner?
How to handle the trade-off between reliability and plasticity in continual learning systems?
How to synergize parametric and non-parametric learning?

claims_to_verify.claim: Anthropic's annualized run rate grew 400 times to $40 billion in under two years.
MIT report states 95% of generative AI pilots at companies are failing.

quotes.text: Intelligence is the capacity to reason through unfamiliar problems from available context.
Expertise is accumulated and situated competence: the ability to act reliably, efficiently, and with judgment to achieve reproducibly superior performance in a particular domain.
Continual learning is adaptive compression of experience into reusable structure for future behavior.

bullets: Intelligence and expertise are orthogonal dimensions in AI systems.
Modern Moravec's paradox explains why AI excels at symbolic coding but struggles with heterogeneous digital micro-worlds.
Continual learning is adaptive compression of experience into reusable structures.
Strong continual learning enables escape intelligence, yielding unbounded expertise from bounded intelligence.
compressed.core_insight: Intelligence gives agents the ability to reason through unfamiliar context, but continual learning is required to compress experience into situated expertise and overcome the limitations of static models.
